subject: Renewal negotiation: safeguard uplift + temporary rate-hold framework
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily@lighthouse.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Liu <mark.liu@lighthouse.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — rate hold & staged uplift request

Jordan,

Our renewal for the inference tier is coming up in mid-August. We've been increasing traffic as we ramp the new product line, but a lot of that is still experimental. Procurement asked me to open the conversation early — two asks from our side: a short-term rate hold through our GA runway and a staged uplift tied to actual usage (so we don't get locked into a steep commit while we're still stabilizing consumption).

If Redwood can provide a 60–90 day price hold and an upfront credit buffer for initial overage months, we can commit to a stepped increase across 12 months (with true-ups each quarter).

I've attached our Q3 forecast and a draft PO so you can see the cadence (Attachment: Lighthouse_Forecast_Q3.xlsx, PO_Lighthouse_Draft.docx). Can we schedule 30 minutes this week to align?

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Head of Procurement
Lighthouse.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — rate hold & staged uplift request

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. 30 min sounds good; I can do Wed or Thu afternoon.

High level response now so you're not waiting: Redwood can consider a timebound rate-hold for an agreed-bucket of usage (60–90 days) plus a staged uplift with quarterly true-ups. Practically we'd structure this as a temporary price hold for the initial ramp window, a committed baseline for year 1 at a reduced uplift, and a credit pool that offsets overage during the first 90 days. We'll need finance and renewals input on the credit sizing and whether the customer wants a rolling true-up or fixed quarterly reconciliation.

Looping in Ben (Director, Strategic Renewals) and Laura (Finance lead) to scope figures and approvals.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Lighthouse renewal — proposed framework and term sheet v3

Team,

Emily sent over the forecast and PO. They want a 60–90 day rate hold and an upfront credit buffer while they stabilize GA traffic. My read: account will commit to a stepped uplift over 12 months but is sensitive to early overages. Proposed commercial approach (draft):

- Year 1: baseline commit = 60% of forecasted run-rate; price = current list less 10% (intro discount)
- Ramp window: 90-day temporary price hold on overage rates at current list (no uplift)
- Credit bucket: $150k credit applied to overage invoices for months 1–3; unused credits roll into Q2 reconciliation but expire at year-end
- Quarterly true-up: reconciliation against actual usage, with a one-way true-up from customer to reach commit; no retroactive price increases during the hold period
- SLA: maintain 99.5% availability for inference endpoints; we include a single remediation credit (not monetary) if SLA missed in ramp period

I've sketched these into TermSheet v3 (attached). Two asks: 1) Ben — is the $150k credit defensible from a renewals standpoint? 2) Laura — can finance accept the roll-forward expiry language for unused credit? Legal will need to check the wording around price hold and true-up mechanics.

I'll prep a short one-pager for Emily ahead of the call if we land on numbers.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive

[Attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Lighthouse renewal — proposed framework and term sheet v3

Jordan — thanks for the draft. My thoughts:

- $150k credit bucket seems reasonable against the headcount and infra they're likely to spin up; it gives them runway without us taking open-ended exposure.
- Prefer 90-day hold vs 60 — their ask included GA runway and product launch dates look tight; 90 gives breathing room and keeps the upward pressure manageable after ramp.
- For the commit baseline, let's set a mechanism: a step-up ladder (60% → 80% → 100%) tied to calendar quarter boundaries, with a single true-up at each quarter close. This avoids continuous micro-true-ups and is easier operationally.
- Approve conditional price hold language so long as legal inserts the normal force-majeure and usage-abuse carveouts.

Operational request: Jordan, can you get Emily to confirm the dates for their GA window and provide a short run-rate snapshot for July/Aug? I'll backstop the credit bucket but would prefer to keep the unused-credit expiry at YE rather than rolling indefinitely.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Renewals | Redwood Inference

[Inline: negotiated bullets for term sheet — will feed into v3.1]
